observation.visible_scene: Outdoor ground covered in dry, pale grass. A hand-drawn cardboard structure (a tower/box with brick and arched-window markings) sits on a flat piece of cardboard laid on the ground. To the left is a heap of gray, curled, already-burnt corrugated cardboard and ash. In the center, a small block of cardboard is actively burning, producing a bright orange-yellow flame. Thin white smoke is visible along the right edge of the cardboard base and behind the box.
visible_changes: The flame continuously flickers and deforms from frame to frame: it alternates between a single tall tongue, a split two-pronged shape, and curled/looping forms, and it leans sometimes left, sometimes right toward the drawn box, but its base stays anchored at the central burning cardboard block.
The pile of gray burnt corrugated cardboard on the left remains essentially static in shape and position throughout the segment.
The drawn cardboard box and the flat base sheet remain in fixed positions; no new charring or collapse of the box is visible within the excerpt.
A faint white smoke plume drifts slowly along the right side of the base and behind the box, changing subtly in density and position.
The camera is largely stationary, with only minor handheld jitter; background grass and boxes keep the same framing across frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the cardboard and how the fire started (the flame is already burning at the first frame).
Whether the drawn box or the left ash pile will eventually catch fire or be consumed.
The state of the scene before t=0 and after t=1.333s, including whether the flame grows, dies, or spreads.
uncertain_details: The exact rate at which the central cardboard block is being consumed is hard to judge; its size looks roughly constant over this short window.
Minor apparent motion of background elements is likely camera jitter rather than object movement, but cannot be fully separated.
Distinguishing the white smoke from the pale cardboard base edge is partly ambiguous in some frames.
